original.prompt: In March 2026, the United States granted India a waiver relating to Russian oil. Consider the following statements:
items: The waiver allowed India to buy Russian oil already stranded at sea for a period of 30 days.
The oil covered by the waiver was estimated to meet about a month of India's oil demand.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told G7 ministers that these cargoes would not benefit the Kremlin because the oil was already loaded.
original.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
original.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Nomura estimated the 20-30 million barrels available would cover just four days of Indian demand, not a month. Bessent also said India would eventually buy more American crude instead, and the US signalled that any further easing would likely be just for India.
original.source: Nomura analysts note the estimated 20-30 million barrels available cover just four days of Indian demand.

rewritten.prompt: In March 2026, the United States granted India a waiver relating to Russian oil. Consider the following statements:
items: The waiver allowed India to buy Russian oil already stranded at sea for a period of 90 days.
The oil covered by the waiver was estimated to meet about a month of India's oil demand.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told G7 ministers that these cargoes would not benefit the Kremlin because the oil had not yet been loaded.
rewritten.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
rewritten.explain: All three statements are wrong: the story says the waiver lasts 30 days, not 90; Nomura estimated the 20-30 million barrels would cover just four days of Indian demand, not a month; and Bessent said the cargoes would not help the Kremlin because the oil was already loaded. Bessent also said India would eventually buy more American crude instead.
rewritten.source: The US granted India a 30-day waiver to purchase stranded Russian oil last Friday at sea, which we covered here.
